description: Fix 1 (highest priority): the create_promise pre-hook becomes enforce-only. It never replaces the amount/date the customer confirmed with its own facts and never writes 'unknown'; it only rejects (blanks the offending field + the product id, guard 'rejected') when a value provably breaks a rule known with certainty, and the post-hook tells the model to state the limit, re-read and re-confirm. Unknown facts pass the value through unchanged. Also the callback hook side of fix 2 (per-weekday windows, callback_hours). Depends on FEAT-001 (p<k>_deadline/p<k>_floor come from the new engine, callback_window_for/callback_hours_text exist). FEAT-003..005 build on the new hook variables.
steps: 2.1 builder/hooks.py: rewrite _PROMISE_PRE_BODY / _PROMISE_POST_BODY exactly as plan section 5 'Fix 1': reset promise_guard/promise_reject/promise_limit_* at the start of every call; keep identity gate + product-id forcing; sent == asked always; reasons date_invalid/date_past/date_after_deadline/date_not_business_day and amount_invalid/amount_above_full/amount_below_floor only when the needed fact is known; reject = blank offending field (date '', amount 0) + blank product id + promise_guard='rejected' + promise_reject + promise_limit_date/amount; unchecked parts listed in promise_unchecked; nothing is ever written as 'unknown'; keep writing promise_changed ('no' / 'rejected'). Post-hook: rejected -> data[ok]=False, p<k>_promise_rejects += 1, within cfg reject_cap (default 2) the text names the limit and requires a new read-back + clear yes (new DEFAULT_TEXTS keys rej_* and T_REREAD), beyond the cap the existing failure path; ok -> p<k>_promise_date/amount from the sent (== confirmed) values; remove the 'values differ' branch. Add optional cfg keys reject_cap and auto_close (auto_close is wired in FEAT-004; accept and ignore it here).

2.1b tests/test_hooks.py: replace the clamp tests (test_promise_date_clamp_agrees_with_engine, test_promise_invalid_date_gets_first_day, test_promise_amount_clamp_agrees_with_classify, test_promise_amount_floor_unknown_and_full_unknown, test_promise_changed_flag, test_promise_post_states_actual_values_when_changed, test_promise_body_field_names_follow_cfg) with scenario tests: facts known+within (unchanged), over deadline (blank + rejected + limit equals engine's last business day <= deadline), below floor / above full / invalid amount (engine.classify_amount agreement, rounding_decimals honoured), not-business-day and past dates (sweep agreement with engine.check_promise_date), facts unknown (floor/deadline/full/business_days empty, garbage now -> pass-through, promise_unchecked set, no body value equal to 'unknown'), a property test over random asked values and random fact states (body value is exactly the asked value or blank/0 with guard rejected; never another non-blank value), post-hook rejected/recorded/cap flows, multi-product per-product limits and id forcing. Keep test_promise_multi_product_id_forcing.

2.2 builder/hooks.py callback hooks: callback_pre_hook accepts cfg['windows'] (list of [weekday_int, hour_start, hour_end, inclusive]) and picks the entry of the date's weekday ((z + 3) % 7 with the existing _to_days); writes vars['callback_hours'] (same text as engine.callback_hours_text) every call; callback_post_hook uses callback_hours in the re-ask text instead of the static HOURS. builder/compiler.py callback_tool passes the windows and the weekday-name list (from engine.WEEKDAYS, never typed). Tests: hook-vs-engine agreement sweeps for a single-window spec and a per-weekday spec (built in test code), callback_hours text equality.

2.3 builder/selfcheck.py: check_promise_dates / check_amounts / expected_promise_date / layout parity follow the new semantics (engine ok/in_range/full -> body unchanged; everything else -> blank + promise_guard 'rejected'); callback cases already use the effective window from FEAT-001. Re-target every mutation test in tests/test_selfcheck.py to the equivalent new hook statement and keep its assertion (amount feature, promise feature, no_none, notes, callback). builder/compiler.py: rewrite TO_VERIFY item 3 (pre-hook only blanks; bank must reject blank date, zero amount, blank product id) and add the new hook variables (promise_reject, promise_limit_date, promise_limit_amount, promise_unchecked, callback_hours, p<k>_promise_rejects) to written_vars; tools_gen.check_default_collisions must stay clean.
Run the contamination script after each sub-step; hook texts are generic English instructions to the model with no brief wording.
acceptance_criteria: For every sweep case the promise pre-hook body is either identical to what the model sent or blanked with promise_guard == 'rejected'; no test finds the string 'unknown' or any different valid value in the body.
With facts unknown the model's value reaches the bank unchanged.
A rejected call makes the post-hook set ok False and instruct a new read-back + clear yes; retries_on_failure is not consumed by rejections.
Recorded p<k>_promise_date / p<k>_promise_amount always equal the asked (confirmed) values.
Callback hook accepts/blanks exactly like engine.check_callback for single and per-weekday windows; callback_hours equals engine.callback_hours_text.
uv run pytest -q passes (>= 679, 0 failures); all selfcheck mutation tests still detect their mutation; contamination script clean.
verification: uv run pytest -q tests/test_hooks.py tests/test_selfcheck.py tests/test_compiler.py tests/test_pipeline_selfcheck.py
findings: FEAT-002 done, nothing committed. pytest 800 passed, contamination 0 hits. Testing kept light per user. Promise pre-hook is enforce-only: resets promise_guard/promise_reject/promise_limit_date/promise_limit_amount/promise_unchecked each call; reasons date_invalid/date_past/date_after_deadline/date_not_business_day/amount_invalid/amount_above_full/amount_below_floor only when the fact is known (reads vars today, business_days, p<k>_deadline/full/floor); reject = blank date '' and/or amount 0 + blank product id + promise_guard='rejected'; promise_changed is 'no'|'rejected'; promise_unchecked lists 'date'/'amount' skipped; never writes 'unknown'. Post-hook: rejected -> data[ok]=False, p<k>_promise_rejects += 1, within cfg reject_cap (default 2) text = DEFAULT_TEXTS reject + rej_* (with <limit>) + reread; beyond the cap the failure path runs WITHOUT retries (retries not consumed by rejections); ok -> p<k>_promise_date/amount = sent (== confirmed). 'differs' text key removed. cfg keys: reject_cap (new), auto_close (documented, accepted/ignored; FEAT-004 must wire it in _PROMISE_POST_BODY and the cfg builder). New DEFAULT_TEXTS keys: reject, reread, rej_date_after_deadline, rej_date_not_business_day, rej_date_past, rej_date_invalid, rej_amount_above_full, rej_amount_below_floor, rej_amount_invalid. Hook const T_REJ = dict of the rej_* texts keyed without the 'rej_' prefix. Callback: callback_pre_hook cfg 'windows' = [[weekday idx (Monday 0), hour_start, hour_end, inclusive|None]] and 'weekday_names' (engine.WEEKDAYS); writes vars['callback_hours'] (== engine.callback_hours_text of callback_dates) when the window has no gaps; callback_post re-ask uses it (falls back to static HOURS). compiler.callback_tool builds windows from per_weekday. compiler: TO_VERIFY item 3 rewritten; written_vars gained promise_reject, promise_limit_date, promise_limit_amount, promise_unchecked, callback_hours, p<k>_promise_rejects. selfcheck: check_promise_dates/check_amounts expect unchanged body for engine ok/full/in_range, else blank + promise_guard 'rejected'. Mutation tests re-targeted: 'mins < hs', 'late = mins > he or', 'asked_date not in bds' -> 'asked_date in bds', promise_changed 'no' -> None (amount mutation 'ac < int(round(floor * 100))' unchanged). Tests: tests/test_hooks.py clamp tests replaced by scenario/property tests; test_compiler.test_scenario_single_promise_recorded now shows reject then accept. Note for FEAT-003/004: the promise_guard var is now always written (''), so any 'guard not in vars' style check must use .get; the callback hook's weekday index uses (days+3)%7.
